mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor or parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the certified extract if required, then obtain an Apostille from the competent Apostille authority in the country of origin. Consular path only for non-Apostille states: notarize, then legalize through the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the country of origin. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the foreign investor or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or relevant government department of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue the official certificate, notarize the issuing officer's signature if required, then attach an Apostille. Consular path for non-member states: issue the certificate, legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate, and attach a certified Korean translation. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

Consular path for non-member states: notarize, legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate, and attach the translation. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and local agents against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, and Korea's KOFIU risk alerts before incorporation. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP status, negative media, residency in FATF-identified high-risk jurisdictions, or opaque nominee structures. All findings must be updated within 24 hours of list updates, documented under Article 5 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, and preserved for seven years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-register) and the Commercial Registration Information System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Hangul; an English or other foreign-language name may be used as a trade name only through a certified Hangul transliteration and must be declared in the articles of incorporation. The registry applies a four-tier review: (i) distinctive name element, (ii) commercial object descriptor, (iii) mandatory corporate form suffix Chusik Hoesa for a stock corporation, and (iv) comparison of identical/deceptively similar names in the nationwide commercial registry within the same line of business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within two weeks of receiving a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the registry court under the Commercial Registration Regulation. The submission must set out the proposed corrected Hangul name, evidence of non-identical pre-existing names, and any ministerial approval if applicable. The court will review the appeal within ten working days; if rejected again, the applicant may apply to the head registrar of the Supreme Court. The original filing fee is carried over only once, and counsel should be engaged for the second-stage appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure commercial mailbox without staff is rejected by the National Tax Service for ordinary place of business registration and by Korean banks for corporate account opening. A virtual office that provides a dedicated rentable meeting room, mail handling, and designated representative services may be accepted, but it is assessed critically because Stripe and Paddle require evidence of the real operating address and business substance. For this AI video synthesis SaaS, the recommended solution is a serviced office with a named desk in Seoul for at least one year.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) physical signage at the registered office; (2) original lease or sublease agreement with the registered agent; (3) local representative available during business hours; (4) tax invoices, accounting books, and the corporate seal at the address; (5) operating assets such as servers, computers, and telecommunication lines; (6) proof of staff employment or an outsourced substance arrangement. Quantified risk: approximately 12% in the first year for a low-risk AIGC SaaS company without statutory licensing; the risk rises to 25% following any VAT invoice mismatch, frequent business relocation, or submission of the same office address by more than 50 unrelated companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as consolidated and amended), particularly Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 300, 301, 317, 318, 334, 409 and 542-6; Commercial Registration Rules; Framework Act on National Taxes Article 168; Registration Tax Act; Local Education Subsidy Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Court Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office of the company (e.g. Seoul Central District Court Registration Office); subsequent business registration is made with the National Tax Service through the local district tax office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for incorporation registration of a stock company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, submitted together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the banker's certificate of deposit of the subscription price.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No statutory minimum paid-in capital exists for a Chusik Hoesa under the amended Korean Commercial Act. However, before filing for incorporation registration, the entire issue price of all shares issued at incorporation must be fully paid in cash to a commercial bank in Korea and evidenced by a certificate of deposit of the subscription price. No separate escrow or blocked account system is required by Korean law, but the deposited amounts may not be withdrawn before registration except in the limited circumstances permitted by the Commercial Act. The bank certificate must accompany the court filing under Articles 301 and 317(2).

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: IROS (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea for name search; a licensed notary public under the Korean Notary Act for notarization of the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a Korea-wide name search for the proposed Korean corporate name and verify that no identical or confusingly similar existing corporate name is registered under the Commercial Act and relevant registration rules. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation specifying the corporate objective of development and supply of AI avatar video generation SaaS, software publishing, cloud services, and related activities, the number of authorized shares, the par value, the total issued shares at incorporation, and the registered office address. All incorporators must sign and affix their seals; the notary must authenticate the Articles. If electronic signatures are used, obtain an accredited digital certificate for each subscriber and ensure it is compatible with the IROS and Hometax portals.
required_dossiers: IROS corporate name search report
Passports or alien registration cards of all incorporators
Personal seal certificates or authenticated signatures
Draft and execution copies of the Articles of Incorporation
Proof of address of the intended registered office
Power of attorney for any agent
Receipt of notary fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected because it is identical or misleadingly similar to an existing corporate name, select an alternative name, rerun the IROS search, and revise and re-notarize the Articles before filing. A correction at this stage does not create a registry penalty because no application fee has been paid to the court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of the Full Subscription Price and Issuance of Banker's Certificate of Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank in Korea designated in the Articles of Incorporation, such as Shinhan Bank, Kookmin Bank, Woori Bank, Hana Bank, or another bank authorized to issue a subscription price deposit certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary pre-incorporation subscription deposit account at the designated commercial bank in the name of the proposed company or as otherwise accepted by the bank, and transfer or remit the full subscription price from each incorporator's account. Verify that the amount deposited is equal to the total issue price stated in the Articles and is paid in cash. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit of the subscription price showing the payer, payee, amount, and payment date; retain the original certificate for the court filing. Do not withdraw the funds before registration, as withdrawal is restricted under the Korean Commercial Act and may invalidate the incorporation. If the contribution is cash only, no external escrow account is required.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of each incorporator
Remittance or transfer instructions from incorporators' bank accounts
Temporary subscription account application form
Bank certificate of deposit of the subscription price (to be issued)
Proof of payment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the certificate due to a discrepancy in the remitter or account name, correct the payment instruction, obtain a bank confirmation letter, and if the designated bank must be changed, amend and re-notarize the Articles. The corrected certificate must then accompany the court filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Application for Incorporation Registration with the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Court Registration Office of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office, e.g. Seoul Central District Court Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks from the date of full payment of the subscription price, file the application for incorporation registration with the competent District Court registry using the forms prescribed by the Commercial Registration Rules. Attach the notarized Articles, the banker's certificate of deposit, the list of shareholders, a statement that all shares have been fully paid, written consents of the directors and auditor, proof of the registered office, and the corporate seal impression. Pay the registration tax, education surtax, and court filing fee at the prescribed rates. The registry verifies compliance with the Commercial Act and the Articles; if a correction order is issued, comply within the fixed period. Upon approval, the court registers the company and issues a certified extract of the corporate registration.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Banker's certificate of deposit of the subscription price
Subscription list and statement of full payment
Written consent of each director and auditor
Proof of registered office address, such as a lease agreement
Copy of incorporator identification
Corporate seal impression form
Payment receipt for registration tax and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, file the required corrected documents within the prescribed period, normally two weeks. If the registration is refused, the applicant may file an administrative appeal or resubmit with corrected facts; legal counsel should be engaged to expedite reconsideration before the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Activation of Bank and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service, through the Hometax online portal or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the corporate registration, file a corporate business registration application with the competent district tax office through Hometax using the company digital certificate. Attach the certified extract of corporate registration, the certified Articles, lease or title documents, and identification of the representative director. The National Tax Service will issue a Business Registration Certificate with the corporate tax number. With this certificate, open the permanent corporate bank account and register for VAT and withholding tax. Enroll the company in the four major social insurance programs for any employees and report the actual place of business. Maintain the corporate seal certificate as the authorized signature instrument for all financial and administrative transactions.
required_dossiers: Corporate business registration application form
Certified extract of corporate registration
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease or title deed
Representative director's identification
Corporate seal certificate
Company digital certificate (accredited)
Bank account opening documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a correction notice, respond promptly through Hometax with the corrected facts or documents. If late registration penalties are proposed because of delay caused by the registry or tax office, submit proof of filing dates and request adjustment or an official deadline extension under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Governance, Seal Registration, and Confirmation of Digital-Only Licensing Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service for tax governance; local district office and local fire station for ordinary office occupancy and fire safety matters.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation and tax registration, complete post-formation governance by preparing the shareholders registry, board minutes, and accounting books. Apply for the corporate seal certificate and register the seal impression with the local government if required. Verify the status of ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210 to confirm that this AI avatar video generation software business is not engaged in manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing, and therefore does not require an industrial operating license, an Environmental Impact Assessment, or a Civil Defense fire permit. For the leased office, confirm compliance with ordinary fire safety, building occupancy, and occupational safety requirements, obtain a fire inspection or occupancy certificate if the landlord or local fire code requires it, and keep documentation in the company file.
required_dossiers: Corporate seal registration application and certificate
Original lease agreement for the registered office
Office floor plan and fire safety inspection checklist
Board minutes and appointment consents
Shareholders register and corporate books
VAT registration and electronic tax invoice confirmation
Digital-only business classification memo based on ISIC 6201
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a public inspector or official erroneously demands an industrial license, submit a written classification opinion showing ISIC 6201 and the National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate indicating software publishing as the sole business purpose. If the fire inspector requires corrective measures, complete the corrective work and obtain a passing inspection before commencing business in the office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. This undertaking is a pure software and AI video generation SaaS business under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility will be established. For ordinary office premises, the local district office and fire station are competent for occupancy and basic fire safety, not an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No statutory operating license, manufacturing permit, or industrial concession is required for software development, cloud-based AI avatar generation, and digital content publishing under Korean law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. Korean Ministry of Environment and its delegated environmental agencies are not engaged because no physical project triggering the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is present.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. ISIC 6201 is a digital software publishing and cloud service activity with no construction, factory, process discharge, wastewater, or emission source; the applicable EIA category is therefore none and no full EIA, preliminary EIA, or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no industrial wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or air emission limits applicable to the software activity. If office equipment is decommissioned, all electronic waste must be disposed of through licensed recyclers under the Waste Management Act; no industrial discharge permit is applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. For the office-based activities of the Company, ordinary fire safety and workplace safety rules under the Fire-Fighting Facilities Installation Act and the Occupational Safety and Health Act apply; a fire inspection or occupancy certificate from the local fire station may be required by the landlord. No Civil Defense manufacturing fire permit is required for a digital AI avatar video generation software company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal at www.hometax.go.kr; the Korea Customs Service at unipass.customs.go.kr handles export clearance for VAT zero-rating evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity, the statutory SOP is: (1) confirm subject status for Korean corporate tax and VAT by examining domestic place of business, permanent establishment, or Korean e-services consumer nexus; (2) appoint a statutory tax representative/certified tax accountant in Korea, where no fixed place of business exists; (3) file the foreign corporation registration application and business registration application with the relevant district tax office via HomeTax, attaching the certified home-country incorporation document, Korean translation of charter, foreign business license, power of attorney, and evidence of domestic place of business or tax representative; (4) obtain the Korean business registration number, which is the tax identification number and VAT registration certificate number; (5) if supplying electronic services to Korean non-VAT persons, complete the HomeTax non-resident electronic service supplier VAT registration workflow using the home-country TIN, email address, and payment settlement evidence; (6) for corporate income tax, if a domestic business establishment is created, file the domestic business establishment registration with NTS; if no domestic business establishment, register only through the domestic withholding agent; (7) maintain all documents and submit e-tax invoice issuance configuration before commencing taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for pass-through or check-the-box characterization; a Korean Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed at the entity level. The only available election is the Korean consolidated corporate tax regime for a qualifying resident parent-subsidiary group, which does not create pass-through treatment or alter indirect tax identity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Korea does not have a turnover threshold that exempts a resident stock corporation or a foreign non-resident electronic service supplier from VAT registration; tax registration is mandatory at the start of business or first taxable supply. An individual with expected annual taxable supplies below KRW 80,000,000 may enter the simplified taxpayer regime, but this is not available to a Chusik Hoesa or to a non-resident corporate supplier of electronic services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices in Korea must be issued as e-tax invoices under the NTS e-Tax Invoice System and transmitted into the HomeTax real-time fiscal clearance server by the business day following supply; issuance requires an official digital certificate and, for large or registered taxpayers, the HomeTax API or EDI channel. The e-tax invoice data are matched with customs export declarations, cash receipts, and payment gateway records to detect under-declaration. For SaaS supplies to Korean consumers, B2C cash receipts are integrated with the same anti-fraud digital stamping framework, and fraud indicators trigger statutory tax investigations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is claimed under the Korean VAT Act when exported goods are transferred out of Korea under a customs export declaration and when services are exported or supplied to a non-resident person outside Korea, including qualifying offshore digital services such as AI avatar video generation SaaS. The supplier must separately identify the zero-rated value in the VAT return and retain evidence proving the overseas destination or recipient, actual use abroad, and the receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident counterparty. For digital services delivered online, the place of supply is treated as the customer's location; supplies to non-residents are zero-rated rather than exempt, thereby preserving the input VAT refund through a VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry), Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service exchange export and VAT data; zero-rating is reversible if the required customs documentation, bill of lading, or foreign exchange settlement certificate is not procured within 180 days. Reversal creates VAT liability, interest, and additional tax penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes, with criminal prosecution for fraudulent refund claims and clawback of refunded input VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates under a liberalized foreign exchange system governed by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Presidential Decree. As of the current regime, the Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions and most capital account transactions are subject to a post-hoc reporting or prior declaration requirement depending on the size and nature. Foreign direct investment, including share acquisition in a Chusik Hoesa, is freely permitted under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with a simple A to E reporting framework through designated foreign exchange banks. Profit remittances in the form of dividends and royalties are permitted once corporate tax and withholding tax obligations are settled, and the remittance must be processed through a domestic foreign exchange bank using designated purpose codes (e.g., 600201 for dividend remittance). There is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW; exporters may maintain foreign currency accounts with domestic banks, but export proceeds must be received within six months from the date of export declaration unless an extension is approved. Capital account transactions, including trade loans and external borrowing, are subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act notification regime, and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) must be updated. The KRW is not fully offshore-convertible for non-residents without a valid underlying trade or investment purpose; non-residents cannot freely borrow KRW outside Korea. Swap and forward transactions are permitted for real exposure hedging, but speculative trading by non-residents is tightly monitored. Overall, the currency is convertible with a robust compliance ecosystem that requires meticulous documentation of the underlying economic substance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 44 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related notices (Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, Articles 23-5), exporters must receive export proceeds within six months of the customs clearance date unless an approved extension is obtained from the MOEF. The proportion of proceeds required to be converted into KRW is effectively zero; exporters are allowed to retain 100% in a foreign currency held account at an authorized domestic bank, provided the receipt is reported to the bank within 30 days. The bank will issue a certified foreign currency receipt confirmation, which serves as the statutory evidence for tax deductions and customs settlement. Non-compliance triggers penalty surcharges and potential restrictions on the entity's foreign exchange banking privileges.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Kookmin Bank (KB Kookmin Bank Co., Ltd.)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, M2, InPay) are legally barred from maintaining demand deposit accounts or issuing local IBAN/KRW routing numbers for South Korean entities without a domestic banking license. The FSC and FSS treat unlicensed financial services as criminal offenses under Article 17 of the Financial Business Structure Improvement Act. Any entity wishing to accept KRW must route through a licensed foreign exchange bank or an electronic financial transaction agent commissioned by a bank. Consequently, using an EMI to receive cross-border SaaS subscription revenue is not feasible for statutory treasury purposes; a direct domestic bank account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The FIU's Enhanced Customer Identification Requirements (Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information) mandate that a newly formed Chusik Hoesa's statutory representative and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) appear for a face-to-face interview at a domestic bank branch or through an in-person video call with a bank officer using ARS-verified mobile identity (accredited by a local telecom operator). A remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Korean Tier-1 banks absent a locally executed power of attorney notarized in Korean and apostilled, with the proxy appearing at a branch for physical identity verification. For foreign embassies in Seoul, a consular officer may not substitute for the bank's direct verification. Thus, the practical mandate is at least one physical appearance by the UBO or a fully authorized director.,,,

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT final return and payment for July 1 - December 31 prior fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 20% additional tax on unpaid VAT plus 0.022% per-day late-payment surcharge; NTS may issue a 30-day compulsory demand and seize funds or assets. Persistent non-filing without business activity may support court-ordered dissolution of a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting of shareholders, including approval of balance sheet, income statement, retained earnings proposal, and auditor report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders in general meeting; company records retained at head office; no government filing required for an unlisted private Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year (within three months after the end of each fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be fined up to KRW 5,000,000 (approx. USD 3,800) for failing to prepare or preserve statutory accounts; failure does not trigger administrative strike-off, but continued corporate dormancy may result in court-ordered dissolution under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (legal entity tax return) with statutory tax reconciliation and audited or unaudited financial statements attached
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; extended to April 30 if the company is subject to external audit and the return is prepared by a licensed tax agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing surcharge of unpaid tax, 10% under-declaration surcharge, 40% surcharge for fraudulent omission, 0.022% per-day late-payment interest, and forced collection by NTS after 30 days from tax demand.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (local income tax on corporate taxable income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (city or county) of the head office jurisdiction through the local tax service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year (within four months after fiscal year end; May 31 if national filing extension applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing surcharge, 0.022% per-day late-payment surcharge, 30-day local tax demand, and compulsory seizure; no direct strike-off but a dormant company may be dissolved by court.

Persistent non-filing without business activity may support court-ordered dissolution of a dormant company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External auditor appointment, audit performance, and board or shareholder approval of audited financial statements (only if statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered external auditor listed on the Financial Supervisory Service external audit registration system; report retained at head office and made available to shareholders at the annual general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Auditor must be appointed not later than March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; audited financial statements must be approved by the ordinary general meeting and the audit report laid before that meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor when required is punishable by an administrative fine of up to KRW 30,000,000 (approx. USD 23,000) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; directors and responsible officers can also be fined for submitting or approving unaudited financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report and UBO event report (applicable only when non-resident ownership is present)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: KOTRA (Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency) or a delegated foreign-exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any transfer, allotment, pledge, or other change in foreign shareholding
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted change report results in administrative fine of up to KRW 1,000,000 and loss of foreign-investment benefits; if registered foreign investment status is cancelled, dividend and exit remittance advantages are forfeited. No separate domestic UBO annual filing exists for a private unlisted software company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private unlisted Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily audited if, at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year, its total assets equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,200,000). Listed companies on KOSPI, KOSDAQ or KONEX are always audited irrespective of size. Companies designated by the Financial Services Commission under Article 2(3) of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, on public-interest grounds, must also be audited. There is no statutory turnover or headcount trigger for an unlisted, non-financial software company; the operative triggers are the balance-sheet asset test, listing status, and explicit FSC designation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) applies to listed companies and financial institutions; a private Chusik Hoesa may prepare statutory financial statements under Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board unless it elects to apply K-IFRS. The Corporate Tax Act requires the financial statements to be reconciled to statutory taxable income in the annual corporate tax return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, non-resident investors holding a recognized foreign investment (generally at least KRW 100,000,000 or 10% equity) must file a change report with KOTRA or a delegated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of every share transfer, pledge, or new issuance. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation return for a wholly domestic Chusik Hoesa; the company must keep the shareholders register current, update it on every share transfer, and comply with shareholder register-inspection rights. If the company were an FIU-regulated financial entity, annual customer beneficial-ownership refresh would apply, but a general AI avatar video generation SaaS company is outside that scope. The binding annual or event-driven protocol is therefore the 30-day foreign-investment change report plus continuous domestic register maintenance.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,000 per annum in the Seoul metropolitan market for a virtual registered address and corporate secretarial support service.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per engagement for a private Korean technology company meeting the KRW 12 billion mandatory audit threshold; smaller review or compilation engagements typically range from USD 3,000 - USD 8,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% effective top statutory marginal rate (22% national corporate income tax plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the 22% national liability; applicable to taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credits of 30-50% for qualified AI avatar and video generation software development under Special Tax Reduction Control Act Article 10; tax exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years for foreign-funded high-tech companies under Article 121-2 of the same act; no standalone patent box regime but AI software development may qualify as new growth industry for preferential credit rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NTS Corporate Income Tax Base and Amount Return (Bub-in-se Gwa-se-pyo-jun mit Se-ae-shin-go-seo) e-filed through the HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; larger taxpayers also must pay first-half estimated corporate tax by September 30.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File no later than 3 months after the fiscal-year closing date; for calendar-year corporations this is March 31. One-month extension may be available on application for companies with overseas accounting difficulties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year, tax district code, corporation identification number, entity name, juridical form Chusik Hoesa, paid-in capital, address, number of employees, business classification ISIC 6201, and foreign ownership ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign investor holding more than 10% must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner and provide a copy of the Tax Residency Certificate; if no Korean permanent establishment is asserted, attach a non-PE position paper and avoid indicating any Korean office or employee in Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from AI video SaaS subscriptions, cloud usage fees, license and maintenance revenue, contract software development (ISIC 6201), and incidental sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean-source business income attributable to a Korean permanent establishment (PE) is taxable under Article 5 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and Article 7 of the OECD-aligned treaty. For no-PE scenarios, report sales as not taxable but retain an independent analysis proving no dependent agent or fixed place in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, cost of goods sold, statutory reserves, dividend received deduction, and intra-group gain elimination.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source dividends received through an intermediate Korean holding entity are excluded only if the participation exemption in the Corporate Income Tax Act is satisfied; any royalty income from overseas related parties must be recognized at arm's length before being put into Box 3.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses including payroll, GPU cloud computing, data storage, AI model training costs, software amortization, communications, marketing, legal and accounting, and overseas travel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties require mandatory evidence in the local file: intercompany agreements, benchmark study, and proof of actual service performance; remittances above the statutory threshold will be disallowed as deductions if an expense certificate such as APTER is not retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after addition of disallowed expenses, subtraction of non-taxable income, and deduction of operating loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation with a Korean PE, taxable income must be computed attributing profits to the PE as if it were a distinct and separate enterprise; directors approving aggressive loss carryforward without supporting standalone financial statements expose the entity to re-audit risk and transfer pricing penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax at the progressive schedule: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% above KRW 20 billion; local income tax added at 10% of the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign corporation elects final withholding on gross Korean-source royalties rather than PE-based net taxation, Box 6 must reflect the 22% final tax and no loss or expense set-off; failure to make this election in writing is treated as PE filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits for foreign taxes paid, R&D credits, temporary investment credits, foreign employment credits, and new growth industry credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claiming treaty foreign tax credit requires attaching the Korean-source tax reconciliation and a certified schedule of foreign taxes; when a Singapore or Hong Kong entity is the recipient, document beneficial ownership to avoid denial of both the treaty credit and the underlying withholding exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld at source during the year, estimated tax prepayments, and withholding from bank interest, dividends, or royalties paid by Korean payers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents receiving payment from a Korean AI platform must have had 22% (20% corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax) withheld on Korean-source dividend, interest or royalty unless a DTA exemption application was lodged with the NTS before or with the payment; attach the relevant declaration and beneficial ownership form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund after deducting prepayments, withholding and non-PE income reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before final submission, confirm that no transfer pricing penalty remains unfunded; NTS domestic and local collections may trigger a director blacklisting or travel ban immediately if the balance exceeds KRW 50 million and the entity fails to pay.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 0.04% per day of unpaid corporate income tax up to 36 months. Unfiled or under-reported items trigger 20% of the additional tax (or 40% for fraud) under Framework Act on National Taxes Articles 47-2 and 47-4; failure to keep transfer pricing and economic substance documentation is subject to administrative fines. Criminal fraud prosecution applies under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act; for corporate officers NTS may blacklist directors on unpaid tax demand lists and bar exit permits under the Economic Crime Prevention Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate outbound dividend withholding tax for non-resident corporate shareholders (20% national Corporate Income Tax as withholding plus 2% local income tax), unless a Double Tax Agreement reduces the rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty-reduced withholding the payee must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction; (2) execute and submit the NTS application for income tax exemption under the tax treaty together with power of attorney and beneficial ownership declaration; (3) attach financial statements evidencing active business and no mere conduit structure; (4) file before or within three months after the payment date; (5) obtain a formal NTS exemption determination. Without TRC and beneficial ownership proof, the Korean payer must withhold 22% and the foreign recipient cannot retroactively claim treaty relief except through refund procedures or the mutual agreement procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding tax is 22% (20% national plus 2% local); statutory royalty withholding tax is 22% on the gross amount. Under major Korean bilateral DTAs the treaty rate for royalties is commonly 10-15% and for interest 10-15%; apply the treaty rate only with a preserved TRC and an economic substance certificate from the revenue authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File is required where cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion per fiscal year; Master File is mandatory where total annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and international related-party transaction amounts reach KRW 5 billion or more. Micro AI SaaS exporters below KRW 5 billion benefit from a documentation exemption but still must keep contemporaneous benchmark evidence.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not impose UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations; however the NTS denies treaty benefits and PE status to a Korean Chusik Hoesa that lacks Core Income-Generating Activities. The CIGA test, derived from Article 7 of the OECD Model and the Multilateral Instrument provisions on preventing treaty abuse, requires that strategic R&D, risk management and AI model evaluation of the avatar video generation product actually occur in Korea. If legal ownership but operational control lies in Hong Kong or another treaty jurisdiction, the NTS will re-allocate income under the substance-over-form doctrine, disregard the Korean entity as a sham, and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Sham and Shell Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Organizing a zero-substance Korean Chusik Hoesa that invoices global AI avatar video license fees, retains no Korean staff, has no R&D activity or board minutes, and shifts 100% of net profit to a low-tax treaty jurisdiction through non-commercial intercompany service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 4 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, intentional under-declaration above KRW 500 million becomes a criminal prosecution: imprisonment of at least 3 years and up to 10 years, plus a fine up to 5 times the evaded tax; the NTS additionally imposes 40% of the underpaid tax as fraud additional tax under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-4.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot hide behind the corporate veil: under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act, a director is personally liable to creditors for wilful or grossly negligent acts. The NTS will blacklist directors and deny exit permits, confiscate foreign bank accounts and real property subject to asset preservation orders, and the director faces the full criminal imprisonment sentence applicable to the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Transfer Pricing and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into controlled AI avatar software licensing transactions with Hong Kong or Singapore related entities at prices materially below cost, or paying royalties to a related party with no development assets or staff; failing to prepare a Local File even though the intercompany threshold was met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS adjusts taxable income under Article 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, adds a 10% transfer pricing penalty under Article 12 of that Act, imposes a 20% under-reporting additional tax, and for excessive intercompany interest applies the thin-capitalization disallowance under Article 24. If intent is shown, a separate tax evasion prosecution is added.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sanctioned the fake intercompany price have civil restitution exposure under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act; a director who personally received the shifted profit is treated as receiving a deemed dividend and subject to progressive tax plus criminal fraud penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act. NTS blacklisting with transfer pricing criminal indicia can be placed before trial and can cancel business permits and visas of foreign directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Return and False Withholding on Non-Resident Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Korean AI SaaS entity remits dividends and royalties to non-resident shareholders or affiliates without operating the 22% withholding tax, or files a corporate income tax return after the 36-month deadline showing no revenue despite Stripe and Paddle payment statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 73 of the Corporate Income Tax Act and the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act, a withholding agent that intentionally fails to withhold incurs a penalty equal to 22% of the amount not withheld, plus daily late filing surcharges of 0.04% and a 20% additional tax for under-reporting. Where evaded tax exceeds KRW 1 billion, the maximum imprisonment is 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for making payments without withholding are jointly and severally liable for all penalties under Article 401 of the Korean Commercial Act; a travel ban and asset freeze are immediately enforceable by the NTS, and the director faces criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for fraudulent non-filing. If tax officials were bribed, the director also faces liability under the Special Crimes Act.
